chapter: Family, marching bands and the tavern
title: Visits from Marvin Johnson and George Orendorff; Charlie Jones
summary: He recalls a Sunday visit from saxophonist Marvin Johnson and George Orendorff and describes Charlie Jones and the Bell Tavern men.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: I remember one time, Marvin Johnson--do you know Marvin Johnson?
Yes I do, a saxophonist.
And George Arndorf came by to see me one Sunday afternoon, the place was just packed. The Clef Club was meeting at Lucas' house.
Don Lucas.
Yes. Not far from where I had my business. So they came by just to say hello to me, I was so busy running back and forth they said, 'Okay I see you're busy, we'll see you later.'
Marvin Johnson was a fine saxophonist too, wasn't he?
He was. I think the first job he and Charlie--him and Charlie Jones was a team, you know, Marvin Johnson and Charlie Jones-- do you know Charlie Jones.
There was a Charles
Martin too.
Charlie Jones, from Rene's band when I first started.
With the now late Leon René.
Charlie left early--Charlie Jones worked out of the Bell Tavern too.
What did he play?
Saxophone, tenor sax. Marvin played the alto and Charlie played the tenor.
Charlie left early, I think it was in the forties, he left and went to --he and his wife-- Sacramento/and had a funeral parlor in Sacramento.
Mortician?
Mortician; yes.
Marvin played locally for many years.
He worked out of the Bell Tavern with us. He was in defense
His wife still lives here in Los Angeles, Iola Johnson.
I saw her not too long ago at the Clef Club Christmas party. Your mother was there.
